anatomy.intro: Fine radial spokes and stronger hooked central spines form two distinct layers around the tubercles.

parts.function: A raised green mound forms part of the water-storing stem.
parts.label: Tubercle

parts.function: Spines emerge from the specialized cushion at the tubercle's tip.
parts.label: Areole

parts.function: Numerous fine pale spokes partly screen the green body.
parts.label: Radial spines

parts.function: A stronger amber-brown spine projects outward with a curved tip.
parts.label: Hooked central spine

flowers.text: M. rekoi has small deep pink to purple-pink flowers with darker midribs. The petal tips flare back, giving the little flowers a distinctive outline.

growth.note: New tubercles appear near the crown. Flowers develop between the tubercles, separate from the spine clusters at their tips.

stages.text: A small rounded body carries tightly arranged tubercles.
stages.title: Bristly globe

stages.text: The stem can elongate while retaining its dense spine covering.
stages.title: Short cylinder

stages.text: Some forms produce offsets in cultivation, although wild plants may remain solitary.
stages.title: Possible clump

habitat.text: Mammillaria rekoi grows in Morelos, Puebla, and Oaxaca, Mexico. It occurs in dry shrubland and can grow on rock, with small globose to short-cylindrical stems.

lookalikes.name: Silken pincushion cactus
lookalikes.text: M. bombycina has a heavier white woolly coat and commonly makes a cluster of cylindrical heads; both can have brown hooked spines.

mature.text: The species has stems roughly 12–15 cm tall and 5–6 cm across. Some forms offset into small clusters.

milestones.text: Purchased at Carlsons' Greenhouse in a 4-inch individual pot.
milestones.title: Joined the collection

milestones.text: Close observations recorded a green rounded body, pale radial spines, and tan-to-red central spines with hooked tips.
milestones.title: Hooked-spine comparison

nameStory.text: The species began as Neomammillaria rekoi in 1923 and was transferred to Mammillaria in 1925.
